verses.text: The Pharisees heard that Jesus was making and baptising more followers than John. When Jesus learned about this,
(although in fact it was not Jesus himself who baptised, but his followers),
he left Judea and went back to Galilee.
On the way he had to pass through Samaria.
So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar. It was near the field that Jacob had given to his son Joseph.
Jacob's well was there. Jesus was tired from the long journey, so he sat down beside the well. It was about twelve o'clock, midday.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Please give me a drink."
His followers had gone into the town to buy food.
The Samaritan woman said to him, "You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?" (She said this because Jews do not usually have anything to do with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered, "If you knew the gift God gives, and who it is that is asking you for a drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
"Sir," the woman said, "you have nothing to draw water with, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water?
Are you greater than our ancestor Jacob? He gave us this well. He drank from it himself, and so did his sons and his animals."
Jesus replied, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water I give them will never be thirsty again. The water I give will become a spring inside them, bubbling up and giving them eternal life."
The woman said to him, "Sir, give me this water! Then I will not get thirsty, and I will not have to keep coming here to draw water."
Jesus told her, "Go and call your husband, and then come back."
"I do not have a husband," the woman replied. Jesus said to her, "You are right when you say you have no husband.
The truth is, you have had five husbands, and the man you are living with now is not your husband. What you have said is quite true."
"Sir," the woman said, "I can see that you are a prophet.
Our ancestors worshipped God on this mountain. But you Jews say that Jerusalem is the place where people must worship."
Jesus said, "Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You Samaritans worship what you do not really know. We Jews worship what we do know, because salvation comes through the Jewish people.
But a time is coming, and it has already come, when true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and in truth. These are the kind of worshippers the Father is looking for.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and in truth."
The woman said, "I know that the Messiah, the one called Christ, is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us."
Then Jesus told her, "I am he, the one speaking to you now."
Just then his followers came back. They were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But none of them asked, "What do you want?" or "Why are you talking with her?"
Then the woman left her water jar, went back into the town and said to the people,
"Come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! Could he be the Christ?"
So the people came out of the town and went towards Jesus.
Meanwhile his followers were urging him, "Rabbi, eat something."
But he said to them, "I have food to eat that you know nothing about."
So his followers asked each other, "Did someone bring him food?"
Jesus said, "My food is to do what God, who sent me, wants, and to finish the work he gave me.
You have a saying: 'Four more months, and then it is harvest time.' But I tell you, open your eyes and look at the fields! They are ripe and ready for harvest.
Even now the person who harvests the crop is being paid. He is gathering a harvest of people for eternal life. So the one who plants and the one who harvests can celebrate together.
This proves the saying true: 'One person plants, and another harvests.'
I sent you to harvest a crop that you did not work for. Others did the hard work, and you have come in to gather the results of their work."
Many Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of what the woman said: "He told me everything I have ever done."
So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them, and he stayed there for two days.
Many more people believed because of what Jesus himself said.
They said to the woman, "Now we believe, not just because of what you told us. We have heard him ourselves, and we know that this man really is the Christ, the Saviour of the world."
After the two days, Jesus left for Galilee.
Jesus himself had said that a prophet is not honoured in his own home town.
When he arrived in Galilee, the people there welcomed him. They had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem during the Passover festival, because they had also been there.
Jesus came once more to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. A royal official was there whose son was sick in Capernaum.
This man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee. So he went to him and begged him to come and heal his son, because his son was close to death.
Jesus said to him, "Unless you people see miraculous signs and wonders, you will never believe."
The official said, "Sir, please come down before my child dies."
Jesus told him, "Go home. Your son will live." The man believed what Jesus said, and he went on his way.
While he was still on his way home, his servants met him with the news that his son was alive and well.
He asked them what time his son had started to get better. They said, "The fever left him yesterday at one o'clock in the afternoon."
Then the father realised that this was the exact time when Jesus had said to him, "Your son will live." So he and everyone in his household believed in Jesus.
This was the second miraculous sign that Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
